_readme: DEVON's manifest of the Hermes agent surface. Generated from the code, never hand typed.

test_devon_hermes_surface.py fails when the code and this file disagree, and also checks the counts fenced in docs/devon/SYS_OPS_devon-hermes-stack-status_v2_2026-08-25.md against the code, so regenerating this file alone cannot clear a failure.

This does NOT mean nothing can slip. Read the 'What it does not cover' paragraph in that document before trusting a green run: raw SQL columns no model declares, rewritten migration bodies under an unchanged revision, and the behaviour behind any tool are all unpinned, and what production actually runs is scripts/estate_reconcile.py, UNVERIFIED without a Railway read.
Regenerate after a deliberate change: PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 -m test_devon_hermes_surface
Then move these records in the same pull request:
2. docs/devon/SYS_OPS_devon-hermes-stack-status_v2_2026-08-25.md, the fenced counts and the capability table
3. a dated docs/devon/SYS_OPS_*.md closing the arc
4. scripts/estate_reconcile.py DOC_CLAIMS, if a pinned sentence changed

Scope: tools from build_tool_registry() across every adapter. Routes from every v1 router prefixed /agent, read from the routers so a route hidden from the OpenAPI schema is still seen. Columns from every agent table under app/models. Migrations that touch one of those tables, and an unparseable migration fails the run rather than being skipped.
